content:
The image shows soybean leaves with a conspicuous white to gray powdery coating covering the leaf surfaces. The coating is dense and uniform, starting as patches that have coalesced to cover entire leaf surfaces. The leaves themselves appear otherwise intact with no necrotic lesions, angular spots, or pustules.

This matches Powdery Mildew precisely: white, powdery coating beginning as small patches coalescing to cover entire leaves.

No signs of:
- Tan/gray tufts on undersides (Downy Mildew)
- Angular water-soaked spots (Bacterial Blight)
- Pustules or raised centers (Bacterial Pustule)
- Rust-colored urediniospore masses (Soybean Rust)
